item.title: Active Issabel CVE-2026-89026 Exploitation and Critical Oracle WebLogic CVE-2026-70756
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Sep 14:00 → 16 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution — Must Read

Issabel Framework users should immediately apply the August 2026 patch for CVE-2026-89026, an actively exploited flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers forge JWTs and execute OS commands through Asterisk.

  • CVE-2026-89026 is a critical Issabel Framework flaw that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary operating-system commands.
  • The flaw stems from a hard-coded HS256 JWT signing key in pbxapi/index.php that was identical across Issabel installations, allowing attackers to forge bearer tokens.
  • Forged tokens can be used with the /pbxapi/manager/originate endpoint and Asterisk's System application to execute commands as the Asterisk user.
  • Issabel patched the issue on August 1, 2026, by replacing the hard-coded JWT key with one stored in /etc/issabel.conf.
  • Shadowserver Foundation first observed active exploitation of CVE-2026-89026 on September 9, 2026, and users are advised to apply the latest fixes.

Products: issabel-framework, pbxapi, asterisk

Vendors: issabel-foundation, vulncheck, shadowserver-foundation

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-70756) Oracle WebLogic Server Takeover via T3 and IIOP — Must Read

Oracle WebLogic Server CVE-2026-70756 is a critical pre-authentication flaw that can allow remote takeover through exposed T3 or IIOP services. Organizations should urgently apply Oracle’s September 2026 CPU and restrict external access to WebLogic listen ports until patching is complete.

  • CVE-2026-70756 is a critical Oracle WebLogic Server flaw with a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 that can allow an unauthenticated network attacker to take full control of a server through T3 or IIOP.
  • Oracle lists WebLogic Server versions 12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0, 14.1.2.0.0, and 15.1.1.0.0 as affected by CVE-2026-70756.
  • WebLogic instances can accept T3 and IIOP traffic on default HTTP listen ports such as TCP/7001 and TCP/7002, including when they appear externally as ordinary web application servers.
  • Oracle released fixes for all affected versions in its September 15, 2026 Critical Security Patch Update.
  • Until patching is confirmed, the article recommends identifying internet-facing WebLogic systems and restricting T3 and IIOP access to trusted internal sources.

Technologies: web-server

Products: oracle-weblogic-server, oracle-fusion-middleware, cycognito-platform

Vendors: oracle, cycognito

item.title: Active ScreenConnect and Pixel Exploitation Lead Identity and Endpoint Threats
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Sep 10:00 → 16 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Critical ScreenConnect flaw now actively exploited in attacks — Must Read

CISA warns that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-84869, a critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect authorization flaw that can enable unauthorized file transfer and execution during remote sessions. Organizations should upgrade to ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later immediately, as more than 1,000 exposed instances reportedly remain unpatched.

  • CISA says attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-84869, a critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaw involving improper privilege management and missing authorization.
  • The flaw can allow attackers with basic privileges to transfer or execute files through active remote sessions without authorization or host confirmation.
  • ConnectWise patched the issue in ScreenConnect version 26.6.5 and later, after previously recommending that teams disable TransferFiles permissions as a temporary mitigation.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-84869 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and directed U.S. federal agencies to secure affected systems within three days.
  • Shadowserver tracked more than 1,000 unpatched ScreenConnect instances exposed online, with most located in North America and Europe.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: screenconnect

Vendors: connectwise

Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation — Must Read

Google patched CVE-2026-58704, a high-severity Pixel cellular modem permission-bypass flaw that may be under limited targeted exploitation. Pixel users should install the September 2026 update with security patch level 2026-09-05 or later.

  • Google disclosed that CVE-2026-58704 is a high-severity privilege-escalation flaw in the Pixel Cellular Modem and may be under limited, targeted exploitation.
  • The flaw is caused by a logic error that can enable a nearby attacker to bypass permissions and gain elevated access without user interaction.
  • Google's September 2026 Pixel updates address CVE-2026-58704 and 109 other security flaws.
  • Google said that applying a Pixel security patch level of 2026-09-05 or later resolves all of the identified flaws.
  • The September update includes 46 critical-severity flaws in Pixel components including BigOcean, Bootloader, IP Multimedia Subsystem, and Trusted Execution Environment.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: pixel, pixel-cellular-modem, android, bigocean, ip-multimedia-subsystem, trusted-execution-environment

Vendors: google

Acronis cPanel Backup Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in Targeted Attacks — Should Read

Acronis says attackers have exploited CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity local privilege-escalation flaw caused by insecure file permissions in its cPanel/WHM Backup plugin. Organizations should immediately update to version 1.9.3 HF3 or later; the related Plesk extension is fixed in build 1.8.11.638.

  • Acronis reported that CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity local privilege-escalation flaw in its Backup plugin for cPanel and WHM, has been exploited in limited, targeted attacks.
  • The flaw has a CVSS score of 7.8 and is caused by insecure file permissions.
  • Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel and WHM on Linux versions before build 1.9.3.1021 are affected, and version 1.9.3 HF3 contains a fix.
  • The Acronis Backup extension for Plesk on Linux versions before build 1.8.11.638 is also affected.
  • An attacker with low privileges could use the flaw to gain greater permissions and potentially perform unauthorized actions or run arbitrary code affecting the application's confidentiality and integrity.

Technologies: backup

Products: acronis-backup-plugin-for-cpanel-whm, acronis-backup-extension-for-plesk

Vendors: acronis, c-panel, plesk

NightEagle targets Russian companies — Should Read

Kaspersky reports that the NightEagle (APT-Q-95) group has expanded from Asian targets to Russian companies, using stolen VPN credentials, the GhostContainer Exchange backdoor, and legitimate tunneling tools to retain access. The group also exploits Active Directory weaknesses and BlueKeep to move laterally, steal credentials, and potentially compromise domain controllers.

  • Kaspersky’s Global Emergency Response Team investigated NightEagle (APT-Q-95) incidents targeting businesses in Russia, expanding beyond the group’s previously reported focus on organizations in Asia.
  • Attackers commonly used compromised valid credentials to access corporate VPNs, with connections originating from Russian IP addresses linked to Cloudflare WARP tunnels and European virtual infrastructure providers.
  • NightEagle deployed the GhostContainer backdoor on Microsoft Exchange servers, using it to process command-and-control instructions, evade security monitoring, and redirect network traffic.
  • The group used Microsoft dev tunnels and rdp2tcp to expose and tunnel Remote Desktop Protocol access, and used Impacket’s atexec utility to create scheduled tasks for port forwarding.
  • In one incident, attackers exploited CVE-2019-0708 (BlueKeep), requested Kerberos tickets with unusual flags, and attempted DCSync activity to obtain domain account password hashes and compromise Active Directory infrastructure.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access, source-control, edr, network-monitoring

Products: microsoft-exchange, microsoft-dev-tunnels, cloudflare-warp, github, kaspersky-threat-analysis, kaspersky-endpoint-detection-and-response-expert, kaspersky-anti-targeted-attack

Vendors: microsoft, cloudflare, github, kaspersky

Atomic macOS (AMOS) Stealer Activity — Should Read

Atomic macOS (AMOS) stealer is an actively evolving macOS infostealer spread through malicious software-installation pages that trick users into pasting commands into Terminal. It establishes persistence, requests access to user data and applications, and exfiltrates credentials, browser data, messaging data, cryptocurrency-wallet information, and other files to changing command-and-control infrastructure.

  • The article analyzes an Atomic macOS (AMOS) stealer infection generated in a lab on August 5, 2026, after a user followed instructions on a malicious website advertising a “macOS toolkit.”
  • The malicious page at getmacouscloud[.]com instructed users to copy and paste text into Terminal, which downloaded a Zsh script and ultimately installed AMOS stealer components.
  • The infection saved persistent files under hidden-looking directories in the user’s Library/Application Support folder, including AccountsHelper and mdworker_shared Mach-O binaries.
  • After the user entered an administrative password, Terminal requested access to Finder, the Desktop and Documents folders, and the Notes application.
  • AMOS collected data into /tmp/out.zip and sent HTTP POST requests to a command-and-control server, with URL paths indicating collection of messengers, credentials, browsers, wallets, and local data.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: macos, terminal, zsh

Vendors: apple, palo-alto-networks

TrustSink: How a Rogue External MFA Provider Steals Passwords — May Read

Varonis researchers demonstrated TrustSink, a post-compromise technique in which a privileged attacker registers a rogue Microsoft Entra External Authentication Method that silently captures users’ plaintext passwords during legitimate MFA flows. Defenders should monitor Authentication Methods Policy and related application changes, remove unauthorized providers before resetting passwords, and restrict privileged identity roles.

  • Varonis Threat Labs demonstrated TrustSink, a technique that uses a rogue Microsoft Entra External Authentication Method provider to capture plaintext passwords during a legitimate sign-in flow.
  • TrustSink requires a Global Administrator or Authentication Policy Administrator account to register the external authentication provider, making it a post-compromise technique.
  • The rogue provider can present a convincing password page to users, record the submitted password, and return a valid signed token that allows the sign-in to complete without an error.
  • Resetting a captured password does not stop TrustSink if the rogue provider remains registered, because it can capture the replacement password at the user’s next sign-in.
  • Defenders should monitor Authentication Methods Policy changes, related application and service-principal creation, unfamiliar provider issuers in sign-in logs, and remove unauthorized providers before resetting affected credentials.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, cloud-platform

Products: microsoft-entra, microsoft-graph, azure-cli, azure-powershell, ngrok, fastapi

Vendors: microsoft, varonis, ngrok, fastapi

Ukraine moves to crack down on scam call centers after corruption scandal — May Read

Ukraine’s parliament approved legislation imposing up to 12 years in prison for organizing, operating or recruiting for fraudulent call centers, following allegations that Prosecutor General’s Office officials accepted bribes to shield such operations.

  • Ukraine’s parliament approved legislation creating separate crimes for electronic fraud, personal or banking data misuse, and establishing, operating, working for, or recruiting people into fraudulent call centers.
  • Under the legislation, people convicted of organizing or working for fraudulent call centers could face seven to 12 years in prison, pending President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s signature.
  • The bill advanced after anti-corruption investigators alleged that Prosecutor General’s Office officials had collected bribes from scam call centers since mid-2025 in exchange for law-enforcement protection.
  • Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau said five people were named as suspects, while former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko denied protecting call centers and has not been charged.
  • Ukrainian authorities reported dismantling a Kyiv call center accused of taking more than $500,000 from dozens of Americans and later shutting down 94 suspected fraudulent call centers during a nationwide operation.

Flock camera use by internal affairs unit puts DC police at odds with officers’ union — May Read

Washington, D.C.’s police union is challenging the Metropolitan Police Department’s use of Flock license-plate-reader cameras to secretly track officers under internal-affairs investigation, citing inadequate controls and transparency. The dispute, headed to arbitration, adds to growing nationwide backlash against Flock’s surveillance technology.

  • The DC Police Union says Metropolitan Police Department Internal Affairs investigators used Flock automated license plate recognition cameras to track sworn officers under investigation without their knowledge.
  • The union filed a complaint seeking to stop the practice, but says MPD denied it and declined to investigate managers involved in the searches; MPD says the dispute is headed to arbitration.
  • MPD said its position is that using license plate reader data in the misconduct investigation was appropriate.
  • DC Councilmember Brooke Pinto asked MPD Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll 10 questions about the department’s use of Flock data and why it needs the technology.
  • The dispute comes amid wider scrutiny of Flock, with Secure Justice reporting that more than 90 U.S. cities and counties stopped working with the company during August.

Technologies: iot-device

Products: flock-automated-license-plate-recognition

Vendors: flock-safety

N0va Phishkit Targets US and EU Businesses: A New Challenge for Identity Security — May Read

The N0va phishing kit targets North American and European organizations by impersonating trusted business platforms and abusing legitimate device-code authentication flows to steal tokens and gain SSO access. Organizations should prioritize identity-focused detection and rapid containment of suspicious authentication activity.

  • N0va targets organizations in North America and Europe, including government, technology, consulting, and healthcare organizations.
  • The phishing kit impersonates business platforms such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, DocuSign, Google Drive, Dropbox, Zoom, and Adobe Sign.
  • N0va can guide victims through legitimate authentication flows, capture access and refresh tokens, and use token exchange or device registration to gain SSO access to corporate resources.
  • A compromised identity can expose email, files, cloud applications, sensitive data, and other business systems, potentially causing financial loss, operational disruption, compliance consequences, and reputational damage.
  • The article promotes ANY.RUN's threat intelligence, interactive sandbox, and threat intelligence feeds as tools for investigating and detecting N0va activity.

Technologies: iam, identity-provider, cloud-platform, siem, soar, edr

Products: threat-intelligence-lookup, interactive-sandbox, threat-intelligence-feeds, microsoft-teams, sharepoint, onedrive, google-drive, docusign, dropbox, zoom, adobe-sign

Vendors: any-run, microsoft, google, docusign, dropbox, zoom, adobe

The Fake IRS Notice That Disproved Itself — May Read

A phishing email impersonating the IRS exposed itself through an impossible CP2000 tax-year claim: it referenced a return that could not yet have been filed or reconciled. The case shows that checking internal inconsistencies in authoritative-looking messages can identify fraud before analyzing links or headers.

  • The phishing email impersonated the IRS and contained conflicting claims about a “2026 filing year” and a “CP2000 Notice - Tax Year 2026.”
  • A CP2000 notice compares a filed tax return with third-party reporting, so the article states that it cannot exist before the return for the named tax year has been filed.
  • The message used the display name “IRS.GOV” on an unrelated sending domain and placed the real recipient only in the envelope and delivery header.
  • The email’s single download button linked to imahdyirs.es, which was behind a shared CDN proxy and returned a 403 response to the scanner.
  • IRONSCALES quarantined the message roughly seven seconds after receipt based on its malicious-link verdict, language and structure analysis, and community resolutions of similar incidents.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis

Vendors: ironscales

EU chief wants joint response to cyberattacks, sabotage — May Read

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed an EU Emergency Security Protocol that would let any member state convene all 27 governments to coordinate responses to cyberattacks, sabotage, arson, and drone incursions. The proposal aims to address escalating hybrid threats but leaves unclear whether it would overcome the EU’s unanimity-based decision-making constraints.

  • European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed an Emergency Security Protocol that would allow any EU member state to call a meeting of all 27 governments after threats such as cyberattacks, sabotage, arson, or drone incursions.
  • Von der Leyen said the proposed protocol would be modeled on NATO’s Article 4 consultation mechanism and would aim to coordinate a European response, deter escalation, and limit an incident’s consequences.
  • The proposal does not specify what governments would do after convening or whether it would change EU foreign and security policy rules that often require unanimous approval.
  • Von der Leyen also announced plans for a European Security Council involving EU leaders and partners including Britain, Canada, Norway, and Ukraine.
  • The Commission plans to include the protocol and other defence initiatives in a forthcoming European security strategy.

Microsoft says Copilot buttons still missing in classic Outlook — Optional

Microsoft is still investigating a Classic Outlook for Windows bug that can make Copilot and Copilot Chat buttons disappear after build 20026.20182. A temporary workaround is to enable “Show Apps in Outlook,” while creating a new Outlook profile or using Outlook on the web also avoids the issue.

  • Microsoft is still investigating an issue that causes Copilot and Copilot Chat buttons to disappear in Classic Outlook for Windows for some users with Copilot Chat (Basic) or paid Microsoft 365 Copilot accounts.
  • Microsoft says the issue occurs after Classic Outlook for Windows is upgraded to build 20026.20182 or later and may prevent Copilot from appearing in the navigation pane.
  • Affected users may find that Copilot is missing above the ribbon or from the app bar, cannot be opened from Add Apps, or appears unavailable when added through ribbon customization.
  • Microsoft’s temporary workaround is to enable the “Show Apps in Outlook” setting under File, Options, Advanced, and Outlook panes; users can also create a new Outlook profile or use new Outlook or Outlook on the web.
  • Microsoft also confirmed that some systems running Kaspersky Antivirus can experience unexpected Outlook crashes associated with the Kaspersky Mail Checker component.

Technologies: antivirus

Products: classic-outlook, microsoft-365-copilot, copilot-chat, outlook-on-the-web, new-outlook, kaspersky-antivirus, microsoft-teams-meeting-add-in

Vendors: microsoft, kaspersky

Securing the unpatchable in an age of AI-driven vulnerabilities — Optional

AI is accelerating discovery of vulnerabilities in legacy, unpatchable OT systems, making passive acceptance of risk untenable. Organizations should compensate with asset visibility, strict micro-segmentation, and upstream NGFW/IPS controls to restrict and inspect the limited traffic these systems require.

  • AI-assisted code analysis is identifying longstanding software flaws, increasing pressure on organizations to apply patches more frequently.
  • Operational technology systems, including medical equipment, building management systems, and industrial systems in chemical plants, may be unable to receive patches because they use certified or unsupported software.
  • When patching is not possible, organizations can identify vulnerable legacy systems, isolate them so only authorized devices can connect, and inspect traffic for known exploit attempts.
  • The 2017 WannaCry outbreak significantly affected the U.K.'s NHS, with a significant minority of systems running end-of-life Windows XP contributing to the problem.
  • Air gaps and one-way data-transfer hardware can be undermined when staff or contractors introduce temporary connections or other operational shortcuts.

Technologies: operating-system, firewall, ids-ips, ics-scada

Products: windows-xp

Vendors: microsoft

Threat Intelligence Alone Won't Close the Exploitation Gap — Optional

The article argues that threat intelligence is most valuable when organizations can rapidly validate whether leaked credentials and disclosed vulnerabilities are exploitable in their own environments. It promotes Pentera and Recorded Future’s threat-led penetration testing integration as a way to automate that validation.

  • The article argues that threat intelligence alerts about leaked credentials and disclosed vulnerabilities often wait in security-team queues before anyone can test whether they are usable in a specific environment.
  • It states that attackers are combining threat intelligence with AI-assisted exploitation to move from exposure to breach faster than many security programs can respond.
  • Threat-led penetration testing starts with current intelligence, such as a particular leaked credential or disclosed vulnerability, and directly tests whether it is exploitable.
  • Pentera's collaboration with Recorded Future connects leaked-credential intelligence to automated testing of an organization's external attack surface.
  • Wyndham Hotels & Resorts participated in early testing of the approach, according to Pentera.

Vendors: pentera, recorded-future

Webinar: What happens in the first hours of a Google Workspace breach — Optional

BleepingComputer and Material Security will host a September 23, 2026 webinar examining real Google Workspace breaches, with a focus on the critical first-hours response decisions that can contain or worsen an incident.

  • BleepingComputer will host a live webinar with Material Security on September 23, 2026, titled "Breach autopsy: How fast-growing companies are breached through Google Workspace."
  • The webinar will feature Material Security Vice President of Security Rajan Kapoor and Fireside Consulting LLC President Rick Fitzgerald.
  • The speakers will examine publicly documented Google Workspace breaches and the decisions organizations made during the first hours of the incidents.
  • Two attacks covered in the webinar involved threat actors combining social engineering with malicious OAuth applications to access Google Workspace environments.
  • The webinar will discuss response decisions, overlooked weaknesses, and security controls that can help fast-growing companies with limited security resources.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: google-workspace

Vendors: google, material-security

Google fixes actively exploited Android zero-day on Pixel devices — Must Read

Google’s September 2026 Pixel update fixes 110 flaws, including CVE-2026-58704, an actively exploited modem vulnerability that can enable nearby attackers with basic device privileges to escalate access without user interaction. Pixel users should install the September security update promptly.

  • Google released September 2026 security patches for Pixel devices that address 110 vulnerabilities.
  • Google said CVE-2026-58704, a high-severity flaw in the cellular modem component, may be under limited targeted exploitation.
  • The modem flaw can allow an attacker on an adjacent network with basic privileges on a targeted device to gain higher privileges without user interaction.

Windows Server 2022 reaches end of mainstream support next month — May Read

Windows Server 2022 will leave mainstream support on October 13, 2026, but will continue receiving free monthly security updates under extended support through October 14, 2031. Microsoft advises organizations to begin planning and testing upgrades to Windows Server 2025.

  • Windows Server 2022 will reach the end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026, and its October 2026 security update will be the final update in that support phase.
  • Windows Server 2022 will receive monthly security updates at no additional cost during extended support through October 14, 2031.
  • Hotpatching for Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition has been extended through October 2027.
  • Microsoft advises administrators to evaluate and test an upgrade to Windows Server 2025 before Windows Server 2022 reaches the end of support.

Products: windows-server-2022, windows-server-2025, windows-10, datacenter-azure-edition

Vendors: microsoft

How to Mitigate the Lethal Trifecta That Infects 98% of Agents — Optional

AI agents become highly vulnerable to prompt-injection-driven data theft when they combine access to sensitive data, untrusted content, and outbound actions. Reduce the risk by separating these capabilities across agents and enforcing least privilege, content inspection, DLP, and action controls.

  • The article describes the AI-agent “lethal trifecta” as the combination of access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to communicate or act externally.
  • When an agent has all three capabilities, malicious instructions in untrusted content can trick it into accessing private data and sending it to an attacker.
  • The article distinguishes prompt injection, which attacks applications built on language models, from jailbreaking, which attempts to bypass protections built into the models themselves.
  • The article recommends designing automation as multiple agents, such as separating a document-reading agent from an action-taking agent that does not directly receive untrusted content.
  • For agents that cannot immediately be redesigned, the article recommends discovering agent capabilities, inspecting incoming content, enforcing least-privilege access and data-loss controls, governing agent actions, and analyzing prompts and responses for malicious instructions.

Technologies: proxy, dlp, api-gateway

Products: ai-command-center, next-gen-secure-web-gateway, agentic-broker, ai-gateway, agent-action-control, ai-guardrails

item.title: Acronis CVE-2026-87886 Exploitation, Oracle CPU, and WordPress Supply-Chain Backdoor
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Sep 18:00 → 15 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Acronis warns of actively exploited flaw in its cPanel backup plugin — Should Read

Acronis warns that CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity local privilege-escalation flaw in its cPanel/WHM and Plesk backup integrations, has been exploited in limited targeted attacks. Administrators should immediately update to Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel & WHM 1.9.3 HF3 or Acronis Backup extension for Plesk 1.8.11.

  • Acronis disclosed CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity local privilege-escalation flaw affecting its backup integrations for cPanel & WHM and Plesk on Linux servers.
  • Acronis says it detected exploitation of the flaw in limited, targeted attacks, based on one report from a potentially affected customer.
  • A low-privileged attacker could use the flaw to gain greater permissions on a vulnerable Linux server, potentially accessing or modifying sensitive data or disrupting the system.
  • The affected Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel & WHM versions earlier than 1.9.3.1021 are fixed in version 1.9.3 HF3, while affected Plesk extension versions earlier than 1.8.11.638 are fixed in version 1.8.11.
  • Acronis has not released technical details or specific indicators of compromise and recommends that affected users apply the available updates immediately.

Technologies: backup, cms

Products: acronis-backup-plugin-for-cpanel-whm, acronis-backup-extension-for-plesk, cpanel-whm, plesk

Vendors: acronis, cpanel, plesk

Oracle September 2026 Critical Security Patch Update addresses 672 CVEs — Should Read

Oracle’s September 2026 Critical Security Patch Update delivers 673 patches for 672 CVEs across 17 product families, including 104 critical-severity issues. Oracle E-Business Suite and Fusion Middleware received the largest share of fixes.

  • Oracle released its September 2026 Critical Security Patch Update on September 15, containing 673 security updates for 672 unique CVEs across 17 product families.
  • The update includes 104 critical-severity patches, 503 high-severity patches, 59 medium-severity patches, and 7 low-severity patches.
  • Oracle E-Business Suite received 159 patches, the most of any product family, followed by Oracle Fusion Middleware with 153 patches.
  • The article reports that 19 Oracle E-Business Suite patches and 78 Oracle Fusion Middleware patches address issues that can be exploited remotely without authentication.
  • Oracle provides patch details in its September 2026 advisory and risk matrices.

Technologies: database, hypervisor

Products: oracle-e-business-suite, oracle-fusion-middleware, oracle-hyperion, oracle-siebel-crm, oracle-analytics, oracle-communications, oracle-commerce, oracle-supply-chain, oracle-virtualization, oracle-peoplesoft, oracle-database-server, oracle-enterprise-manager, oracle-java-se, oracle-autonomous-health-framework, oracle-utilities-applications

Vendors: oracle, tenable

Malcious Admin Menu Editor Pro plugin backdoors 1,500 WordPress sites — Should Read

A compromise of the Admin Menu Editor Pro update server distributed trojanized versions 2.35 and 2.36, installing web shells and hidden WordPress users on potentially more than 1,500 sites. Customers should restore from a known-safe backup or remove the malicious plugin files, object-cache directory, and associated database entries.

  • An unauthorized party compromised adminmenueditor.com and distributed malicious Admin Menu Editor Pro versions 2.35 and 2.36.
  • The malicious updates included a file that installed a web shell and created a hidden WordPress user account on affected sites.
  • The developer estimates that at least 230 customers installed the initial malicious update across at least 1,500 sites, while the total may be higher because version 2.36 was also compromised.
  • The developer took the website offline after concluding that the attacker likely had root-level server access.
  • Users of versions 2.35 and 2.36 are advised to restore from a safe backup made before September 14 or remove the plugin, object-cache directory, and identified database entries.

Technologies: cms

Products: admin-menu-editor-pro, admin-menu-editor, wordpress

Vendors: janis-elsts, wordpress

KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials and Session Tokens — Should Read

Elastic researchers uncovered KREMLIN, a Brazilian banking-malware operation that installs malicious Chrome and Edge extensions to steal credentials, session tokens, cookies, and browser data. The campaign uses multi-stage loaders, SentinelOne DLL sideloading, Chromium preference-integrity bypasses, and Ethereum smart contracts to rotate its command-and-control infrastructure.

  • Elastic Security Labs identified a Brazilian banking-malware operation tracked as REF9334 that has been active since at least May 2025 and delivers a toolkit called KREMLIN.
  • KREMLIN uses document-themed JavaScript files to launch multi-stage loaders, then installs a malicious Chrome or Edge extension named “AVSync System Inc.” that steals credentials, session tokens, cookies, browser storage, screenshots, and page contents.
  • The operation uses Ethereum smart contracts to retrieve changing command-and-control and payload-hosting locations, complicating efforts to disrupt its infrastructure.
  • KREMLIN bypasses Chromium extension protections by modifying Secure Preferences, enabling developer mode, and generating forged metadata to register its malicious extension.
  • Elastic registered KREMLIN’s network-canary domain and observed 1,515 infected systems checking it, with more than 98% geolocated in Brazil.

Technologies: browser, edr

Products: google-chrome, microsoft-edge, sentinelmemoryscanner

Vendors: google, microsoft, sentinelone, elastic, ethereum

Silent Push Tracks a Mass Phishing Operation Through Fast Flux — Should Read

Silent Push identified a large phishing ecosystem using fast-flux DNS services to rapidly rotate IP infrastructure and evade takedowns, including campaigns impersonating Canadian banks and international financial brands. The operators combine DNS rotation with traffic cloaking, per-victim URLs, live credential theft, callback scams, and gated malware downloads to defeat automated scanning.

  • Silent Push reported that it purchased a fast-flux service to observe its operation and used the resulting detection approach to identify thousands of live phishing domains.
  • The identified infrastructure rapidly rotates a domain across IP addresses and networks, which makes IP-address blocking less effective.
  • One phishing cluster targeted nearly 2,000 domains, with roughly nine in ten impersonating Canadian organizations such as major banks, the tax authority, Canada Post, and provincial benefit programs.
  • The Canadian banking campaign used Keitaro traffic distribution software to filter visitors, showing phishing pages to selected Canadian residential users while many other visitors received a 404 page.
  • A second cluster combined fake fraud hotlines, cloned login forms, live chat, and one-time-code-gated downloads of a Windows executable presented as a security verification tool.

Technologies: proxy, network-monitoring

Products: total-view, iofa, keitaro, dnspod

Vendors: silent-push, keitaro, dnspod, media-land

Norway announces investigations into telecom Telenor’s work with Myanmar junta — Should Read

Norwegian authorities are investigating Telenor over allegations that it enabled Myanmar junta repression by providing customer traffic data after the 2021 coup and by selling sanctioned surveillance equipment without authorization during its Myanmar exit.

  • Norway’s National Criminal Investigation Service is investigating whether Telenor was complicit in crimes against humanity by repeatedly providing Myanmar’s military regime with customers’ historical traffic data between the February 1, 2021 coup and the March 25, 2022 sale of its subsidiary.
  • Norway’s Police Security Service is investigating whether Telenor violated sanctions because its sale of the Myanmar subsidiary included sanctioned surveillance equipment without permission from Norway’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
  • Norwegian law enforcement raided Telenor’s Oslo headquarters, while Telenor said its employees risked imprisonment, torture, or the death penalty if they did not comply with military orders.
  • Telenor sold its Myanmar business to Lebanon’s M1 Group in 2022, after which M1 sold 80% of the operation to Shwe Byain Phyu, a company run by allies of Myanmar’s military government.
  • Human rights groups and a Swedish nonprofit have brought legal cases alleging that Telenor-shared data was used by Myanmar’s junta to locate, detain, torture, and in at least one alleged case execute people.

Products: telenor-myanmar

Vendors: telenor, m1-group

Mythic C2 Activity at Internet Scale — May Read

Censys identified 131 internet-exposed Mythic C2 hosts, most recognizable through default TLS certificates and port 7443 behavior. While some deployments appear to be labs, others show sophisticated operational infrastructure, making these fingerprints useful for proactive network and host-based detection.

  • Mythic is an open-source, plugin-based command-and-control framework used in authorized security testing and observed in unauthorized intrusions.
  • As of September 11, 2026, Censys tracked 131 unique publicly exposed hosts matching Mythic detections, with 115 presenting certificates whose subject organization was "Mythic" or "Mythic C2."
  • Port 7443 appeared on 99 tracked hosts, and Mythic's default Nginx reverse proxy returns an HTTP 502 response to unauthenticated requests on that port.
  • Ten of the 131 tracked hosts also exposed at least one additional command-and-control framework, including Sliver, Adaptix C2, Havoc, or FRP.
  • Censys recommends that defenders monitor for Mythic default certificate names, the CN=operators to CN=multiplayer certificate chain, and unexpected Mythic Docker container names.

Technologies: container-platform, web-server, message-queue, cloud-platform

Products: mythic, apollo, sliver, adaptix-c2, havoc, frp, nginx, rabbitmq

Vendors: censys, mythic-community, digitalocean, amazon-web-services, microsoft

item.title: Iranian Telegram Spyware, BambooToken MQTT Malware, and CenterPoint Data Theft
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Sep 14:00 → 15 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Iranian Hackers Use Telegram-Controlled Malware to Spy on Dissidents and Journalists — Should Read

U.S., U.K., and Dutch agencies say Iran’s MOIS is using Telegram-controlled Windows malware, tracked as HEAVYGRAM/CHOSEN BRICK, to spy on dissidents, journalists, and activists. The malware is delivered through impersonated apps and can steal messages and credentials, record audio, capture screenshots, evade Defender, and potentially wipe infected systems.

  • U.S., U.K., and Dutch agencies say Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security uses Windows malware tracked as HEAVYGRAM by the FBI and CHOSEN BRICK by the U.K. National Cyber Security Centre.
  • The campaign has targeted Iranian dissidents, opposition journalists, activists, and other people whose views conflict with the Iranian government, including people in the United States, United Kingdom, and Netherlands.
  • Attackers impersonate trusted contacts or messaging-app support and send files disguised as legitimate software, including Pictory, KeePass, Telegram, RunwayML, Norton Antivirus, Adobe Flash Player, and MRI scan results.
  • After installation, the malware uses a dedicated Telegram bot for each infected computer and can collect emails, chat data, saved passwords, screenshots, microphone recordings, and additional files.
  • The malware establishes persistence through a Windows registry Run key, can exclude folders from Microsoft Defender scanning, and may send stolen data through Telegram and cloud-storage services such as Vultr and Storj.

Technologies: operating-system, antivirus, cloud-platform, object-storage, proxy

Products: telegram, windows, microsoft-defender, vultr-object-storage, storj

Vendors: telegram, microsoft, vultr, storj

Hackers target WordPress sites via third-party WooCommerce plugin — Should Read

Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-27540 in WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture versions 2.0.3.1 and earlier to upload PHP webshells and potentially take over WordPress sites. Administrators should upgrade to version 2.0.3.2 or later and check for suspicious PHP files, AJAX requests, and unknown admin accounts.

  • CVE-2026-27540 is an unauthenticated file-upload flaw affecting WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture plugin versions 2.0.3.1 and earlier for WordPress.
  • The flaw lets attackers alter a user-controlled upload setting to allow PHP files, enabling them to upload webshells that can execute code on the affected site.
  • WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture version 2.0.3.2, released on February 20, fixes the vulnerability.
  • Wordfence said its web application firewall blocked more than 100,000 attacks associated with CVE-2026-27540, with activity spiking between June 4 and June 17 and again on July 1 and August 30.
  • Administrators are advised to update the plugin, inspect upload directories and logs for suspicious activity, remove unknown administrator accounts, and restore from a safe backup if compromise is confirmed.

Technologies: cms, waf

Products: wordpress, woocommerce-wholesale-lead-capture, wordfence

Vendors: wordpress, defiant

How Money Laundering, Scams, and Espionage Hide in a Web Full of Casino Garbage — Should Read

Infoblox found that millions of lookalike casino websites conceal distinct criminal operations, including illegal gambling and money laundering, scam gambling, and China-aligned PeckBirdy malware C2 infrastructure. Defenders should not dismiss casino or adult-domain activity as policy violations, because repeated queries to multiple PeckBirdy C2 domains may indicate a compromise.

  • Infoblox separates malicious casino websites into three groups: illegal Chinese-language gambling sites used for gambling and money laundering, scam gambling sites that prevent victims from withdrawing funds, and PeckBirdy decoy sites used for malware command-and-control communications.
  • Infoblox tracks more than 1.7 million illegal Chinese-language casino domains, with the FUNNULL and Vigorish Viper networks accounting for roughly 81% of that population.
  • China-aligned APT groups have used the PeckBirdy framework since 2023 to embed command-and-control domains in low-quality Chinese-language casino and adult websites.
  • The PeckBirdy domain mcp-source[.]online had zero VirusTotal detections as of August 2026, despite being used for WebSocket connections from some PeckBirdy decoy sites.
  • Infoblox found that just over 3% of its enterprise customers resolved at least one PeckBirdy command-and-control domain, and repeated resolution of three to ten distinct such domains may indicate a potential compromise.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: peckbirdy

Vendors: infoblox, trend-micro, amazon, microsoft, cloudflare, google

CenterPoint Energy confirms customer data stolen in cyberattack — Should Read

CenterPoint Energy confirmed that an unauthorized party accessed personal information for an undetermined number of customers through an external-facing system, following claims that 7.49 million records were stolen via an inadequately protected public API. The company says utility operations were unaffected and is investigating, strengthening defenses, and preparing required notifications.

  • CenterPoint Energy confirmed that an unauthorized third party obtained personal information related to some customers through an external-facing system.
  • A threat actor using the alias “4d722e4d656f77” claimed to have stolen 7.49 million CenterPoint customer records and leaked the data after alleging the company ignored its messages.
  • The alleged stolen records included names, phone numbers, service and billing addresses, account numbers, billing amounts, and partial Social Security numbers.
  • CenterPoint Energy said its electric and gas services were not affected and that it does not expect the incident to materially affect its business or financial condition.
  • The company has engaged third-party cybersecurity experts, strengthened system protections, and reported the incident to law enforcement and regulators while it investigates the scope of affected data and customers.

BambooToken malware controls Windows and Linux systems via MQTT — Should Read

Researchers uncovered BambooToken, a cross-platform malware framework that uses MQTT broker topics for stealthy command-and-control of Windows and Linux systems. The campaign has compromised roughly a dozen organizations, largely in Asia and South America, and may be consistent with China-aligned activity.

  • BambooToken is a previously unknown malware framework active since at least 2023 that uses MQTT to communicate with infected Windows and Linux systems.
  • BambooToken variants developed between 2024 and 2025 use MQTT topics tied to a unique identifier to receive attacker commands and send status and system information.
  • Researchers said BambooToken was delivered by side-loading through digitally signed Tendyron OnKey USB-token software or by impersonating Kingsoft Office.
  • A Linux BambooToken 2.1 sample observed in December 2025 can collect system information, open a command shell, and upload, download, or delete files, although researchers said it appeared to be under development.
  • Lumen identified about a dozen compromised enterprise entities, primarily in Asia and South America, and reported that a GitLab server in Hong Kong was also compromised.

Technologies: message-queue, source-control, operating-system

Products: tendyron-onkey, kingsoft-office, gitlab

Vendors: lumen, tendyron, kingsoft, gitlab

Zelensky appoints former police chief to lead Ukraine’s cyber coordination center — May Read

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed former police chief and interior minister Ihor Klymenko to lead the National Cybersecurity Coordination Center, which coordinates government responses to major cyber threats. The move is part of a broader reshuffle of Ukraine’s security leadership amid ongoing Russian cyber operations and criminal-network threats.

  • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed former law enforcement official Ihor Klymenko to lead the National Cybersecurity Coordination Center.
  • The National Cybersecurity Coordination Center operates under Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council and coordinates government responses to major cyber threats.
  • Klymenko previously headed Ukraine’s National Police, which includes the country’s cyber police department, and later served as interior minister.
  • The center, created in 2016, monitors cyber threats, coordinates cybersecurity agencies, and oversees Ukraine’s national cybersecurity strategy.
  • Klymenko’s appointment is part of a broader reshuffle of Ukraine’s security and law enforcement leadership.

HTM Workflow Tweaks to Secure Devices — Optional

Health-ISAC argues that healthcare technology management teams should embed cybersecurity checks, such as password and software-version verification, into routine preventive maintenance to improve medical-device safety, availability, and resilience.

  • Healthcare technology management professionals are responsible for maintaining the reliability, safety, and performance of medical devices used by clinicians.
  • The article states that preventive maintenance helps ensure equipment functions as intended, while cybersecurity activities help ensure devices remain trustworthy, available, and safe for patient care.
  • Cyber-resilience should be incorporated into normal healthcare technology management workflows rather than treated as a separate activity.
  • Routine maintenance provides opportunities for teams to check passwords and verify software versions as part of strengthening medical-device cyber-resilience.

item.title: Ransomware Exploits VMware vCenter CVE-2026-59310 as Vite and Marimo Attacks Expand
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Sep 10:00 → 15 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA: Critical VMware RCE flaw now exploited by ransomware gangs — Must Read

CISA says ransomware groups are now exploiting the critical VMware vCenter Syslog Server directory-traversal RCE flaw CVE-2026-59310, which was patched in July and added to the KEV catalog. Organizations should urgently patch exposed vCenter systems, as attackers have already used the flaw to establish reverse SSH access.

  • CISA has flagged CVE-2026-59310, a critical VMware vCenter Syslog Server flaw patched by Broadcom on July 29, as actively used in ransomware campaigns.
  • The flaw is a directory-traversal issue that unauthenticated attackers can use to run arbitrary code on affected vCenter systems.
  • QUIRSO reported that a suspected advanced persistent threat actor compromised more than 361 IP addresses in 47 countries and deployed a reverse SSH tool after exploiting the flaw.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-59310 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and required U.S. government agencies to secure affected vCenter systems within three days.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 450 VMware vCenter servers exposed to the internet, though the number patched against this flaw is unknown.

Technologies: hypervisor, remote-access

Products: vmware-vcenter-server, vmware-vcenter-syslog-server, vmware-esxi

Vendors: broadcom, vmware

Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds — Should Read

Sysdig observed a skilled attacker exploit the critical Marimo RCE flaw CVE-2026-39987 and pivot to an SSH bastion using AWS Secrets Manager credentials in just eight seconds, demonstrating that human operators can match AI-assisted attack speed while evading common traps.

  • Sysdig reported that a threat actor exploited CVE-2026-39987, a pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaw affecting all versions of Marimo, to gain an interactive shell.
  • After gaining access, the operator used credentials harvested from the compromised instance to call AWS Secrets Manager, retrieve an SSH private key, and authenticate to a bastion host in eight seconds.
  • Sysdig said the attacker ran more than 850 interactive commands during a nine-hour session and used hand-written scripts rather than recognizable public offensive tools or an AI agent.
  • Hunt.io identified a cryptomining campaign compromising 3,562 Redis servers, with rogue Redis replication used to deploy an XMRig miner.
  • Hunt.io said the Redis victims ranged from Redis 2.8.17 through 7.2.0 and that missing authentication, rather than a version-specific flaw, appeared to be the primary weakness.

Technologies: secrets-manager, cloud-platform, database, cms, iot-device

Products: marimo, aws-secrets-manager, redis, wordpress, mongodb, dahua-ip-cameras, xmrig

Vendors: sysdig, hunt-io, marimo, amazon-web-services, redis, automattic, mongodb, dahua-technology

Mass-Scanning Campaign Exploits Vite Flaw to Extract Cloud Credentials From Exposed Dev Servers — Should Read

Attackers are mass-scanning internet-exposed Vite development servers to exploit CVE-2026-39364, bypassing file-deny rules with query parameters to steal .env files, cloud credentials, and infrastructure configuration data. Organizations should patch Vite and ensure development servers are not publicly exposed.

  • F5 Labs observed an automated campaign in August 2026 that scanned internet-exposed Vite development servers to steal cloud credentials, configuration files, and infrastructure state files.
  • The campaign exploits CVE-2026-39364, a Vite flaw with a CVSS score of 8.2 that can allow unauthenticated requests with query parameters such as ?raw or ?import&raw to retrieve files blocked by server.fs.deny.
  • An application is affected when its Vite development server is exposed to a network, the sensitive file is within directories allowed by server.fs.allow, and the file matches a server.fs.deny rule.
  • Observed requests targeted environment files, AWS credentials and configurations, Terraform state files, Azure profiles, and system paths including /etc/passwd and /proc/self/cwd/.env.
  • The malicious requests used spoofed crawler and AI-bot User-Agent headers and forged X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP values, with significant activity originating from the United States, Belgium, the Netherlands, Singapore, and Taiwan.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: vite, amazon-web-services, microsoft-azure, google-cloud-platform

Vendors: vite, f5, amazon-web-services, microsoft, google

ParaShells: Parallels Desktop Turns Appliance Install Into a Root Shell — Should Read

JFrog researchers found that Parallels Desktop 26.4.0 can let any low-privileged local macOS user gain root by abusing its world-writable privileged service socket and an argument-injection flaw in appliance extraction. The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-90894, was fixed in Parallels Desktop 27.0.0.

  • JFrog researchers found that Parallels Desktop 26.4.0 build 57513 on Apple silicon allowed a non-administrator local user to execute code as root through the prl_disp_service helper.
  • The attack uses the world-writable /var/run/prl_disp_service.socket, where an unsigned local client can successfully use PrlSrv_LoginLocal without Parallels code signing.
  • A quote in the appliance installation parent path can inject a tar option that causes macOS tar to run an attacker-controlled program with root privileges.
  • The issue is tracked as CVE-2026-90894 and was fixed in Parallels Desktop 27.0.0.
  • The article states that a running virtual machine is not required for the proven attack path, provided the privileged helper and its socket are present.

Technologies: hypervisor, operating-system

Products: parallels-desktop, prl-disp-service, macos

Vendors: parallels, apple, jfrog

Have it both ways: stay discoverable in search while disallowing AI training — May Read

Cloudflare launched a Disallow AI Training control that lets site owners block AI model training while preserving search indexing for accountable mixed-use crawlers such as Googlebot, Applebot, and Bingbot. The setting publishes no-training preferences through robots.txt and expands Cloudflare’s bot controls across search, training, and agent behavior.

  • Cloudflare introduced a Disallow AI Training setting that publishes a no-training preference in robots.txt while allowing accountable mixed-use crawlers to continue indexing sites for search.
  • Under the new controls, selecting Block or Block on pages with ads applies to mixed-use crawlers such as Applebot, Bingbot, and Googlebot and can therefore affect search discoverability.
  • Apple, Google, and Microsoft are designated Accountable because they provide or have committed to provide controls for AI training and AI summaries, transparency, and assurance that training opt-outs do not affect traditional search results.
  • Cloudflare states that training-only crawlers operated by Amazon, Anthropic, Meta, and OpenAI can be blocked without affecting search because those organizations separate search and training crawlers.
  • Cloudflare plans to develop controls by early next year that let site owners manage how much of their content is included in AI summaries through a single Cloudflare setting.

Technologies: waf, cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-bot-management, ai-crawl-control, bot-preference-sync, cloudflare-radar, applebot, googlebot, bingbot

Vendors: cloudflare, apple, google, microsoft, amazon, anthropic, meta, openai

Manhattan DA takes down 12 AI deepfake porn sites — May Read

The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office seized 12 domains hosting AI-generated non-consensual pornography involving more than 1,200 people, and says its investigation remains ongoing. Prosecutors warned that deepfake abuse can facilitate harassment and domestic violence, and will monitor for replacement domains.

  • The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office seized the domains of 12 AI deepfake pornography websites for allegedly violating laws on disseminating non-consensual videos.
  • The sites hosted AI-generated videos involving more than 1,200 people and allowed users to use real people’s faces and bodies to create pornography.
  • District Attorney Alvin Bragg said the office knows of domestic violence cases in which partners threatened to release deepfake images of victims.
  • Bragg said the investigation is ongoing and that his office will monitor for attempts to revive the platforms under new domains.
  • Microsoft sued six developers last year over alleged use of Azure OpenAI services to create non-consensual intimate images and sexually explicit content.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: azure-openai, grok

Vendors: microsoft, x

The Renewal Notice for a Domain That Could Not Be Renewed — May Read

A phishing email impersonating Squarespace used a real but dormant company domain to create urgency, yet public registration data showed the domain was already renewed, held by a different registrar, and registry-locked against renewal. The key lesson is to verify domain expiry, registrar, and status codes independently before acting on renewal notices.

  • In late August 2026, a shared partnerships mailbox at a global digital advertising agency received a Squarespace-branded domain renewal email seeking $12.47 for a legacy domain.
  • Public registration data showed that the named domain had been renewed months earlier, was paid through the following year, and was registered with a registrar unrelated to Squarespace.
  • The domain had registry status locks including clientRenewProhibited, meaning the registry would reject any attempt to renew it until the lock was removed.
  • The email authenticated through SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for the attacker-controlled sending domain, while impersonating Squarespace through a display name, organization header, postal addresses, and a branded destination domain.
  • The sole Renew Domain link used a Google shortlink that resolved to a malicious Cloudflare-fronted squarespace.one destination, whose content was not observed because the attacker’s bot protection blocked the scanner.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: squarespace-domains, google-workspace, adaptive-ai, exim

Vendors: squarespace, google, cloudflare, ironscales, gname, exim

China spy chief points at US AI models in cyber threat warning — May Read

China’s intelligence chief warned that U.S. AI models Anthropic Claude Mythos and OpenAI GPT-5.5-Cyber could accelerate vulnerability discovery and malware development, posing risks to China’s critical infrastructure, without alleging either had been used against China.

  • Chen Yixin, head of China’s Ministry of State Security, named Anthropic’s Claude Mythos and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5-Cyber as examples of AI models that could accelerate vulnerability discovery and malware development.
  • Chen did not accuse either U.S. AI model of having been used in attacks on China.
  • Chen said generative AI could be used to fabricate political rumors, spread harmful information, and incite confrontational sentiment at low cost and large scale.
  • Anthropic reported days earlier that a Chinese-speaking group used Claude in what the company described as an autonomous vulnerability research program that found several zero-day flaws in a major security product.
  • China’s Cyberspace Administration released updated AI-governance guidance focused on autonomous agents and embodied AI, identifying loss of control as a core risk.

Products: claude-mythos, gpt-5-5-cyber

Vendors: anthropic, openai

1Password's AI patching benchmark is misleading — May Read

Trail of Bits argues that 1Password’s 26% AI clean-patch headline is misleading because it combines unusually difficult bugs, deliberately wrong instructions, and trials where agents could not test fixes. Its reanalysis found agents blocked the supplied exploit in 86% of reasonably configured trials, while emphasizing that both AI and human fixes require rigorous validation and review.

  • Trail of Bits argues that 1Password’s reported 26% clean-fix rate combines deliberately incorrect repair instructions and trials in which agents could not build or test their patches.
  • After excluding trials that prohibited testing, instructed agents to apply the wrong fix, or consulted the upstream fix, Trail of Bits found that 2,634 of 3,067 generated patches, or 86%, blocked the supplied exploit.
  • Trail of Bits’ review of 2,265 first fixes submitted by developers across 236 security assessments found that 283 first fixes, or 12.5%, did not fully resolve the reported issue.
  • Of 186 closed or merged Patch the Planet pull requests examined by September 14, 2026, maintainers merged 126, and accepted the originally proposed security fix in 91 of those merged pull requests.
  • Trail of Bits released post-patch-validation and review-walkthrough skills to help agents test security fixes and help engineers review code changes.

Technologies: message-queue, operating-system, browser, web-server

Products: flawed, patch-the-planet, post-patch-validation, review-walkthrough, gpt-5-5, opus-4-8, activemq, linux, chromium, freenginx, go-jose, noble-curves

Vendors: 1password, trail-of-bits, openai, anthropic, apache, chromium-project, freenginx, go-jose, paulmillr

Australia is replacing the Essential Eight with a new cyber framework. Here’s how exposure management can help you get ahead of it. — Optional

Australia’s ASD is replacing the Essential Eight with an outcomes-based Essentials series that will require organizations to demonstrate their security posture continuously across enterprise IT, cloud, identity, and OT. The article argues that continuous exposure management can help organizations prioritize and evidence current cyber risks rather than rely on periodic compliance snapshots.

  • The Australian Signals Directorate announced in June 2026 that it will replace the Essential Eight with an outcomes-focused Essentials series, with deprecation targeted to begin around mid-2027 and full retirement around mid-2028.
  • The Essential Eight was designed for on-premises enterprise IT and assessed eight named controls at periodic maturity levels, while the new Essentials series is intended to cover enterprise IT, identity, SaaS, cloud, and operational technology.
  • The first Essentials chapter, covering enterprise IT, reached public consultation in July 2026, while timelines for cloud, operational technology, and potential agentic AI chapters have not been set.
  • The article argues that periodic compliance reports can become outdated quickly in environments where cloud services, identities, SaaS applications, and connected operational technology change frequently.
  • Tenable states that its Tenable One Exposure Management Platform can combine exposure information across multiple environments to help organizations identify critical risks, attack paths, and changes in security posture.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: tenable-one, essential-eight, essentials-series, microsoft-365, google-workspace

Vendors: tenable, australian-signals-directorate, microsoft, google

Give every teammate and agent the right level of access to your Workers — Optional

Cloudflare has launched resource-level access controls for Workers, allowing teams and agents to receive narrowly scoped roles for a specific Worker rather than broad account-wide permissions. The new roles support least-privilege debugging, code review, deployment, and administration, with similar controls planned for D1, R2, and KV.

  • Cloudflare has introduced Worker-level access controls that let customers give a user or API token access to a specific Worker rather than to all account resources.
  • The four new roles are Metadata Read-Only, Content Read-Only, Editor, and Admin, and they can be assigned at the Developer Platform, product, or individual resource scope.
  • Metadata Read-Only permits access to Worker settings, metrics, logs, traces, and analytics without exposing source code, while Content Read-Only permits code review without modification or deployment.
  • An Editor token scoped to one Worker can deploy changes to that Worker but cannot delete it or modify other Workers, helping limit the impact of a misconfigured or exposed CI/CD token.
  • Changing a Worker route or Custom Domain requires both Editor access to the Worker and Workers Routes permission for the relevant zone.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database, object-storage, ci-cd, iam

Products: cloudflare-workers, durable-objects, cloudflare-d1, cloudflare-r2, cloudflare-kv, wrangler, terraform

Vendors: cloudflare, hashicorp

Introducing Varonis Data Lifecycle Management — Optional

Varonis launched Data Lifecycle Management, a capability that identifies redundant, obsolete, and trivial data across connected environments and automatically quarantines it using data sensitivity, permissions, activity, and retention context. The company positions it as a way to reduce storage costs, compliance exposure, and AI quality issues without irreversible deletion.

  • Varonis introduced Data Lifecycle Management, a capability designed to automatically find and quarantine redundant, obsolete, and trivial data across an organization’s data estate.
  • The article states that at least 30% of enterprise data is redundant, obsolete, or trivial, contributing to storage costs, degraded AI results, and increased exposure of sensitive information.
  • Varonis Data Lifecycle Management is built on the Varonis Data Security Platform and uses information about data sensitivity, permissions, and activity to identify data that is stale, duplicated, overexposed, or past its retention window.
  • The product provides a unified dashboard for viewing redundant, obsolete, and trivial data, including duplicate clusters, stale files and folders, and data past its retention window.
  • When data violates configured policies for duplicates, staleness, or retention, Varonis automatically moves it to a secure quarantine, and the action can be reversed before deletion.

Technologies: dlp

Products: varonis-data-lifecycle-management, varonis-data-security-platform

Vendors: varonis

What Zero-Day Response Should Be in the Post-Mythos Era — Optional

Sponsored by Picus Security, the article argues that organizations should validate likely attack techniques and compensating controls immediately after a zero-day disclosure rather than wait for a patch or public exploit. It promotes combining exploitability validation, breach-and-attack simulation, and controlled real-exploit testing to close exposure gaps at machine speed.

  • PaperCut said on August 27 that attackers were already exploiting PaperCut NG and MF servers before a CVE, public exploit, or patch was available, and its third emergency patch was released September 1.
  • The article argues that organizations can test the likely steps of an attack, such as delivery, execution, privilege escalation, process injection, and credential access, even when no working exploit is publicly available.
  • In the article's hypothetical scenario, security-control testing identified missed delivery, non-blocking web-application firewall detection, and absent endpoint and SIEM alerts, then prompted rules and hardening changes.
  • After threat intelligence linked the hypothetical CVE-2026-1001 to an Iranian group, a wider attack simulation found a missed persistence technique that was subsequently addressed.
  • The sponsored article promotes using exploitability validation, security-control validation, and agentic pentesting together to respond to zero-day vulnerabilities before patches are available.

Technologies: firewall, waf, edr, siem

Products: picus-platform, papercut-ng, papercut-mf

Vendors: picus-security, papercut

Attack Chains, Not Just Attack Surfaces: Why Testing Individual Techniques Misses the Point — Optional

Filigran argues that security validation should test end-to-end attack chains rather than isolated techniques, since attackers combine phishing, credential abuse, lateral movement, and exfiltration to exploit gaps between controls. Its OpenAEV platform promotes automated, conditional attack-chain simulations—including AI-assisted autonomous execution—to continuously identify the chokepoints that would stop a real intrusion.

  • The article argues that testing individual security techniques does not show whether a real attacker could combine multiple steps into a successful intrusion.
  • Filigran's State of Threat Management report is cited as finding that 93% of security leaders reported a business-impacting cyberattack in the prior 12 months, while 84% cited siloed tools and disconnected testing as a reason exposures go unnoticed.
  • The article describes Attack Chaining in Filigran OpenAEV as a way to automate multi-stage attack simulations in which the results of one step determine the next step.
  • OpenAEV attack chains can use defined boundaries for assets, targets, permitted actions, and escalation limits, according to the article.
  • The article says XTM One can enable an AI agent to plan, execute, and adapt an attack chain from an operator-defined objective and scope.

Technologies: orchestration

Products: openaev, xtm-one

Vendors: filigran

The Defensible AI-SOC: SOC Modernization for the Mythos Era | Corelight — Optional

Corelight promotes a “defensible AI-SOC” approach to SOC modernization, emphasizing the need for trustworthy, explainable security operations as AI-driven threats and tooling evolve.

  • The article is titled “The Defensible AI-SOC: SOC Modernization for the Mythos Era.”
  • The article concerns modernization of security operations centers, or SOCs.
  • The article presents the concept of a “defensible AI-SOC.”
  • Corelight is identified as the article’s publisher.

Cisco patches Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks — Must Read

Cisco has patched CVE-2026-76461, a critical zero-day in Secure Email Gateway email parsing that is actively exploited to execute root-level commands remotely. Organizations should apply updates immediately and review mail, network, and firewall logs for signs of malicious SQL statements or suspicious external transfers.

  • Cisco patched CVE-2026-76461, a critical Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day that it says threat actors have actively exploited since at least September 2026.
  • The flaw affects Cisco AsyncOS Software on physical and virtual Secure Email Gateway appliances regardless of configuration and can let an unauthenticated remote attacker execute commands with root privileges.
  • Cisco said the issue stems from insufficient validation in email parsing, allowing a crafted email containing malicious SQL statements to trigger arbitrary SQL execution and operating-system command execution.
  • Cisco provided indicators of compromise and advised administrators to inspect mail_logs for suspicious SQL statements and review network and firewall logs for suspicious transfers to or from external or malicious IP addresses.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-76461 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and directed U.S. federal agencies to patch affected systems by September 17.

China-linked groups UTA0560 and JungleBamboo exploited a Chrome and Windows patch gap through spear-phishing links to deploy GRIMWEDGE and LONGTALE malware against NGOs. The campaign shows how publicly visible Chromium fixes can remain exploitable as zero-days in Chrome until stable releases ship.

Mythic C2 Activity at Internet Scale — May Read

Censys identified 131 internet-exposed Mythic C2 hosts, most recognizable through default TLS certificates and port 7443 behavior. While some deployments appear to be labs, others show sophisticated operational infrastructure, making these fingerprints useful for proactive network and host-based detection.

  • Mythic is an open-source, plugin-based command-and-control framework used in authorized security testing and observed in unauthorized intrusions.
  • As of September 11, 2026, Censys tracked 131 unique publicly exposed hosts matching Mythic detections, with 115 presenting certificates whose subject organization was "Mythic" or "Mythic C2."
  • Port 7443 appeared on 99 tracked hosts, and Mythic's default Nginx reverse proxy returns an HTTP 502 response to unauthenticated requests on that port.
  • Ten of the 131 tracked hosts also exposed at least one additional command-and-control framework, including Sliver, Adaptix C2, Havoc, or FRP.

The Renewal Notice for a Domain That Could Not Be Renewed — May Read

A phishing email impersonating Squarespace used a real but dormant company domain to make a fake renewal demand seem credible, despite public records showing the domain was already renewed, registrar-locked against renewal, and held by another registrar. The case shows that checking a domain’s expiry, registrar, and registry status can quickly disprove renewal lures without clicking links.

  • In late August 2026, a shared partnerships mailbox at a global digital advertising agency received a Squarespace-branded email demanding $12.47 to renew a legacy domain by the following day.
  • Public registration information showed that the named domain had been renewed months earlier, was paid through the following year, and was registered through a registrar unrelated to Squarespace.
  • The domain’s registry status included a renew-prohibited lock, meaning the registry would reject any renewal request until the lock was removed.
  • The email authenticated with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for the attacker-controlled sending domain, but those checks did not authenticate the Squarespace brand used in the message.
  • The email’s Renew Domain link used a Google shortlink that resolved to a malicious Squarespace-branded domain, while the destination blocked the scanner from observing its page content.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed former police chief and NSDC head Ihor Klymenko to lead the National Cybersecurity Coordination Center, which coordinates government responses to major cyberthreats including Russian operations.

  • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed former law enforcement official Ihor Klymenko to lead the National Cybersecurity Coordination Center.

China’s top intelligence official warned that advanced U.S. AI models, including Anthropic’s Claude Mythos and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5-Cyber, could accelerate vulnerability discovery and cyberattacks against critical infrastructure, without alleging either had targeted China. The warning accompanies China’s broader push for tighter AI governance and criticism of U.S. export controls and closed-source AI ecosystems.

  • Chen Yixin, head of China’s Ministry of State Security, warned that generative AI could threaten China’s political, institutional, and ideological security by enabling large-scale fabrication of rumors and harmful information.
  • Chen cited Anthropic’s Claude Mythos and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5-Cyber as examples of AI capabilities that could speed vulnerability discovery and malware development, but did not allege either model had been used against China.
  • Chen said cyber operations are entering a phase of industrialized vulnerability discovery, automated attack-and-defense activity, and AI-versus-AI competition, creating risks for China’s critical information infrastructure.
  • Anthropic reported days before Chen’s article that a Chinese-speaking group used Claude for an autonomous vulnerability research program that found several zero-day flaws in a major security product.
  • The Cyberspace Administration of China released updated AI governance guidance focused on autonomous agents and embodied AI, identifying loss of control as a core risk.

Microsoft confirms KB5002914 Excel update breaks copy and paste — May Read

Microsoft confirmed that the September 2026 KB5002914 security update can silently break copy, paste, autofill, and formula dragging in Excel 2016 through 2024. The company is investigating, while affected users report that uninstalling or rolling back the update restores functionality.

  • Microsoft confirmed that the September 2026 KB5002914 security update can cause copy and paste to silently fail in Excel 2016, 2019, 2021, and 2024.

The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office seized 12 AI deepfake pornography websites that allegedly hosted non-consensual sexual images and videos of more than 1,200 people. Cloudflare has launched resource-level access controls for Workers, allowing teams and agents to receive narrowly scoped roles for a specific Worker rather than broad account-wide permissions. 1Password's AI patching benchmark is misleading — Optional

Trail of Bits argues that 1Password’s 26% AI clean-patch headline is misleading because it mixes deliberately wrong prompts and no-testing trials with normal repair attempts. Its reanalysis found 86% of appropriately configured agent patches blocked the supplied exploit, while emphasizing that both AI and human fixes still need rigorous validation and review.

  • Trail of Bits argues that 1Password’s reported 26% clean-fix rate is misleading because it combines difficult handpicked vulnerabilities, trials with prompts that instructed agents to apply wrong fixes, and trials where agents could not build or test their patches.
  • In a reanalysis limited to trials where agents could run code and were not told to apply a wrong fix, Trail of Bits found that 2,634 of 3,067 patches, or 86%, blocked the supplied exploit.
  • Trail of Bits reviewed first fixes for 2,265 vulnerabilities from 236 security assessments and found that 283 first fixes, or 12.5%, did not fully resolve the reported issue.

Netskope has launched Skylight AI Security, a unified suite within its Netskope One platform for discovering, governing, and protecting enterprise AI use. The release includes Agent Action Control, which can classify and allow, alert on, or block risky AI agent actions before they execute.

Microsoft releases emergency Windows updates to fix RDS failures — Should Read

Microsoft released emergency out-of-band Windows updates to fix Remote Desktop Services failures caused by September 2026 security updates across affected Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server systems. The updates also address certain Hyper-V shared-folder and multichannel USB audio issues, though some USB Audio Class 1.0 problems remain unresolved.

  • Microsoft released emergency out-of-band Windows updates on September 14 to address Remote Desktop Services failures caused by September security updates.
  • Affected systems experienced Remote Desktop connection and sign-in failures, and some servers became unresponsive; related tools such as Microsoft Management Console, File Explorer, and Windows Update could also stop responding.
  • The updates include KB5129236 for Windows 10 21H2 and 22H2, KB5129195 for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2, KB5129194 for Windows 11 26H1, and separate updates for Windows Server 2019, 2022, and 2025.
  • The Windows 11 out-of-band updates also fix a Hyper-V folder-sharing issue involving Linux virtual machines and certain multichannel USB audio failures.
  • Microsoft says some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices may still fail to start or produce audio after the September 8 security update, and it is working on a further fix.
